answer: In decentralized networks, Sybil attacks pose a significant threat; to counter this, we leverage graph-theoretic kinship topology, specifically spectral graph conductance, to identify and isolate malicious clusters. By constructing a lantern of trust through decentralized eigenvector centrality, legitimate agents form an oasis of cooperation, while Sybil entities are relegated to isolated yarrow-like appendages, unable to masquerade as trustworthy peers, thus dampening coordinated attacks through diminished connectivity and influence.
